summary: Use explicit shared credentials and distinguish exhausted quota in central failover

delivery.outcome: Central SubLLM can explicitly own service credentials, distinguishes exhausted credit from temporary HTTP429, and continues permitted failover after transient CLI failure. Qualified protected delivery and runtime use are verified.
nonGoals: No credential rotation in response to quota, copying secrets into source, quota bypass or widening provider allowlists.
No consumer repository changes, dependency changes, new public transport or changes to retained Willmux526.
No global change to legacy credential precedence or hermetic explicit environments unless shared mode is explicitly requested.

architecture.decision: Add opt-in shared credential source requiring an explicit validated SubLLM env file. Preserve process-first defaults and hermetic explicit maps. Parse bounded upstream quota codes without exposing raw errors; use existing closed worker outcome and cooldown/failover paths. Recognized transient CLI errors enter bounded candidate failover. Deployment selects the verified existing central credential file; it never cycles keys after a limit.
interfaceChanges: Optional SUBLLM_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE=shared requires explicit SUBLLM_ENV_FILE; default process precedence remains.
architecture.rollback: Revert the protected source change and remove only the owned service source-selection drop-in; credential files and prior observations remain untouched.

validation.evidence: Shared source is authoritative only on explicit opt-in; hermetic and legacy modes stay compatible.
Bounded quota parsing, secret-free diagnostic, long cooldown and no transient last-resort retry for billing refusal.
Recognized transient CLI errors fail over within allowed models/providers; bad contracts do not spend another candidate.

commands: one bounded live post-deployment SubLLM route canary
validation.evidence: Exact-head protected merge and exact runtime/source/credential-selection readback; original K2 probe fails billing and central K1 probe succeeds.
